title: Oxygen-Hemoglobin Dissociation Curve: Clinical Shifts
subject: Physiology
preview: A right shift of the oxygen–hemoglobin dissociation curve favors oxygen unloading to tissues.
quickRevision: A right shift of the oxygen–hemoglobin dissociation curve favors oxygen unloading to tissues.
Fetal hemoglobin and carbon monoxide exposure alter oxygen binding behavior in clinically different ways.
Pulse oximetry alone does not fully describe oxygen content or tissue delivery.

sections.title: Core biomedical mechanism
points: A right shift of the oxygen–hemoglobin dissociation curve favors oxygen unloading to tissues.
Increased carbon dioxide, higher temperature, lower pH and increased 2,3-BPG commonly shift the curve right.

sections.title: Clinical application
points: Fetal hemoglobin and carbon monoxide exposure alter oxygen binding behavior in clinically different ways.
Pulse oximetry alone does not fully describe oxygen content or tissue delivery.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: A higher hemoglobin saturation at a given partial pressure does not automatically mean better tissue oxygen delivery.

quiz.question: Which change usually shifts the oxyhemoglobin curve to the right?
quiz.explanation: Increased temperature. Increased carbon dioxide, higher temperature, lower pH and increased 2,3-BPG commonly shift the curve right.
